Maintaining realtalk

Source: .github/MAINTAINING.md
  1. Open the automatic data update PR. To create one manually, run Actions → Draft update on main.
  2. Click Approve and run workflows if asked. Wait for passing checks.
  3. Read the memo. If correct, select Files changed → Review changes → Approve.
  4. Run Actions → Publish update on main. Wait for it to finish.

Review and publish

Check the memo’s data coverage, revisions, unexpected revisions, FRED comparison, and stale inputs. Investigate anything unexpected before approving.

The realtalk-maintainers team approves PRs and runs releases. Anyone with Write access can draft updates and start PR checks. Authors cannot approve their own PRs.

Publish update merges the data PR, checks the merge commit, and creates a release. The release publishes to r-universe and updates the website. Merging alone publishes nothing. Do not create releases by hand; that skips checks.

The workflow asks r-universe to sync. Allow about 10 to 15 minutes.

How data drafts work

  • Calendar refresh: Mondays, 5:17 a.m. Eastern. Saves BLS and BEA release dates on the calendar branch.
  • Scheduled data update: daily, 10:17 a.m. Eastern. Drafts on release days and rebuilds open drafts after main changes. GitHub can start runs late.
  • Draft update: fetches data, compares with FRED, sets the version and NEWS.md, checks the package, and updates the data-update PR. If data matches main, it closes any old data PR.

Automatic runs keep approval if processed data and the base commit are unchanged. Manual drafts always replace the draft and remove approval.

Do not edit data-update by hand. Merge fixes through a separate PR to main, then run Draft update again.

Versions use the draft date in Eastern time, YYYY.M.D, plus .1, .2, etc. if needed.

New data check manually checks for newer data and manages the new-data reminder issue. Merging the data PR also closes the reminder.

For previews, select dry_run in Draft update, Calendar refresh, Scheduled data update, or either release workflow. This leaves branches, issues, and releases unchanged. Real runs use main.

Other changes

Use an ordinary PR for code fixes and hand-maintained data in data-raw/raw/static/ (CPI-U-RS, CPI-U-X1, and the minimum wage).

  1. Make the change on a branch and rebuild the affected outputs. To publish it, update Version in DESCRIPTION and add a NEWS.md entry.
  2. Get maintainer approval and passing checks. Merge with a merge commit.
  3. To publish, run Actions → Tag release on main. It checks and releases the current main by default.

Admins can merge their own PR without another approval, but the required check must pass.

If an update fails

Problem Action
Calendar or schedule fails Rerun Calendar refresh, or use Draft update manually. Failed refreshes notify maintainers and keep the old schedule.
Download fails or expected data is missing Retry Draft update later. Old source data can produce no PR or notification. There is no automatic retry.
FRED comparison fails Investigate the named series and month.
Publish update refuses Follow the error. If main changed, draft again and review again.
Publish update fails after merging Select Re-run failed jobs. Alternatively, run Tag release with the merge commit from the failed run’s summary.
r-universe sync warns or times out The release exists. Try the sync button or inspect builds.

If the sync request fails, r-universe can take a few hours to find the release.

Setup and settings

  • Secrets: set BLS_API_KEY, BEA_API_KEY, FRED_API_KEY, and BLS_DOWNLOAD_EMAIL in repository settings. The email is the BLS calendar download contact. Local calendar refreshes need the same environment variable.
  • First calendar run: run Calendar refresh with dry_run, check the dates in the summary, then run it without dry_run. Keep the calendar branch. Run Calendar refresh manually if an agency changes a date before the next Monday.
  • Code owners: .github/CODEOWNERS must name @economic/realtalk-maintainers. The team must be visible and have Maintain access.
  • Rulesets (Settings → Rules): “protect main” requires a PR, one code-owner approval, dismissal of approvals after new commits, and merge commits only. It blocks force pushes and deletion; admins can bypass it for PRs. “require check on main” requires check to pass, with no bypass.
  • r-universe: keep "branch": "*release" for realtalk in economic/economic.r-universe.dev’s packages.json.
